findings.claim: The how-to and ADR 0025 say that after a kmctl release with no template change, `uvx copier update` changes nothing. It does change something: copier rewrites `_commit` in .copier-answers.yml to the new tag, so the project gets a one-line diff to commit at every release. That is the cost the operator accepted, so the docs should say so.

The how-to's table still describes the generated .pre-commit-config.yaml as 'Generic hooks only'. It does not mention the new exclude, which leaves the agent files APM and kmctl plugin patch install (.agents/, .claude/agents|rules|skills/, .opencode/, opencode.json) unchecked. A user who adds a hook and sees it skip those files has nothing to explain why.

verdict.text: The change does what the plan says.
copier.yml sits at the root with `_subdirectory: starter`.
starter/ matches kmctl-starter's template/ except for the planned `exclude:` in .pre-commit-config.yaml (checked with diff -r).
The validator now accepts a, b and rc tags.
`release.py set` moves kmctl_ref's default, lists copier.yml among the files it wrote, and refuses without writing anything when the default is missing.
release.yml stages copier.yml, and CI gains a starter job.
Every eval row's test asserts its fails_when.
My stamp is green.
Two small doc fixes remain, neither blocking.
My `loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree: lint, format, tests and integration all pass, and so do eval rows r1, r2, r3, r5, r6, r7, r8 and r9.
Ran `diff -r starter /home/vscode/kmctl-starter/template`: only .pre-commit-config.yaml differs, by the exclude and its comment.
copier.yml against kmctl-starter's: only the header comment, `_subdirectory`, the help sentence and the validator regex and message changed.
Tested the `_COPIER_DEFAULT` regex against the real copier.yml.
It matches only kmctl_ref's `  default:` line, and it cannot cross into another top-level key, because the lines it skips must start with whitespace.
With that line removed it finds nothing, so `set` refuses.
For pre-release tags, the validator's version check turns '0rc1' into 0 through Jinja's `int` filter.
So v0.6.0rc1 passes, and an OpenCode pin on v0.5.1rc1 is refused, which is right because it comes before v0.5.1.
Eval rows, test by test: r1 compares the exact set of files a render writes against GENERATED, so a stray kmctl file fails it.
It also checks targets, the apm entry, the justfile and CI pins, and that the YAML parses.
r2 compares the default with apm/apm.yml's version.
r3 checks both refusals and their messages, including that the OpenCode one names v0.5.1, and that both accepted cases render with their ref.
r5 checks the line-set difference, the file listing, that the refusal leaves a clean git status, and the git add line.
r6 checks that the lock's resolved_commit and uv's direct_url commit_id equal the clone's HEAD, so the package and the CLI provably came from the clone.
It also checks that doctor's failures are limited to UNPASSABLE.
r7 checks the setup-uv step, the just install and the exact last command.
r8 checks the phrases, the links, that only the move section names the old repository, the decision schema and the decision's content.
I also ran `kmctl check` (all checks passed) and okf validate --strict (conformant) myself.
Read the release.py, conftest `tree_repo`, the CI and release workflows, the fixture changes, README, the manifesto, the overview and ADR 0025.
No claim in them contradicts the code, apart from f1.
f1 (docs, not blocking): the docs say "`uvx copier update` then changes nothing", but update rewrites `_commit` in .copier-answers.yml.
Say that a release with no template change only moves `_commit` there.
The same sentence is in the how-to's "Keep a project current" section and in ADR 0025's Consequences.
f2 (docs, not blocking): in the how-to's "What a generated project holds" table, the `.pre-commit-config.yaml` row should say that the hooks skip the agent files APM and kmctl plugin patch install.
The starter CI job is the first CI job to run the `consumer` fixture and real uvx and APM installs.
It cannot be checked until it runs on GitHub, as the plan's Done line expects.
While reviewing I ran `git add -N .` in the worktree by mistake, which marks the new files intent-to-add in the index.
File contents are unchanged.
The review freeze stopped my `git reset`, so the implementer may want to run `git reset` before committing.
